# Fixture provenance: TDS on loans on one side, and TDS debits, in `loans_interest` (#1875 rules 3 and 4)

Every book named here is invented, with round figures and plain names. No fixture is a Tally read of any real assessee. No new fixture file is added: the books are unit tests in `src/loans_interest.rs` on typed inputs, plus four existing edge books whose goldens move.

`docs/tax-audit/parity-spec-v1.md` section 12 requires every change to an existing output to be a declared difference that names the invented book which exercises it. Both rules below were decided by the owner on 31 Oct 2026 and are to be recorded on #1875. The reference engine is not changed and still reads both shapes as before.

## Declared behaviour difference: TDS on loans on one side (#1875 rule 3)

A voucher that posts to the loan and to another configured loan used to count its TDS for neither loan. That still holds, except for one shape, shape (a): every posted line is on a configured loan or a TDS ledger, the loan lines are all on one side, and the TDS lines net to their sum (Loan 1 Dr 8,502 / Loan 2 Dr 164.25 / TDS Payable Cr 8,666.25). Each loan then takes its own line as its TDS, in `tds_on_loan_<tag>`, so LOAN-1 ties on each. A nil line is no posting here, as elsewhere since #1259. Loans on opposite sides are a transfer between loans, a row on each (bridge#803), and are not this shape.

Shapes (b) and (c) keep LOAN-1 as #1259 left it. In (b), a voucher whose lines on the loan net to nil carries the loan's interest and TDS. In (c), a voucher both credits and debits the loan and carries TDS (`edge-books/loans_interest_two_sided_tds.json`, and Seen Loan and Under Loan in `edge-books/loans_interest_phase_a_s194a.json`). LOAN-1 still fires on both, and neither golden's module check moves.

- Unit tests: `tds_on_two_loans_on_one_side_is_each_loans_own_line` (shape (a), with and without a nil bank line); `tds_on_two_loans_not_of_shape_a_counts_on_neither` (opposite sides, another posted line, TDS short of the loans' sum); `loan_1_still_fires_on_a_zero_net_loan_voucher_carrying_tds` (shape (b)); `loan_1_still_fires_on_a_two_sided_loan_voucher_carrying_tds` (shape (c)).
Rule 3 never makes a pass. A loan's own line on such a voucher says nothing of how the deduction divides between the loans' interest, so where one is counted in `tds_on_loan_<tag>` the s.194A coverage reads a new value, "not checked", never "covered" or "covered by amount, not by date". The coverage figure's text then lists that reading, and `tds_on_loan_<tag>`'s text names each such voucher and says the loan's own line is counted, not the voucher's TDS lines. Where the interest is over the threshold, the s.194A finding lists the loan for clause 21(b), titled "TDS on the loan not checked against the s.194A rate", with the limit "Not checked: whether the TDS on <voucher>, split across loans on one side, covers this interest.", and the loan counts in `s194a_tds_over_threshold_lender_count`. No TDS-seen finding fires for it. Where the rules carry no s.194A rate, or the coverage is not computed, those readings stay. A split voucher whose loans are credited is a debit (rule 4 below).

- Unit test: `tds_split_across_loans_is_never_read_as_covering_the_interest`. A person lender's interest of 85,020 (Interest A Dr / Loan A Cr), then Loan A Dr 8,502 / Loan B Dr 164.25 / TDS Payable Cr 8,666.25: coverage "not checked", no `s194a_tds_seen/` finding, the loan listed with the limit and counted. The control, the same deduction on Loan A alone, reads "covered" with the TDS-seen finding.
- `edge-books/loans_interest_tds_coverage.json`, Twin A and Twin B: one TDS journal debits both loans 10,000 paise each against TDS Payable Cr 20,000 paise. The golden now carries `tds_on_loan_<tag>` 10000 for each, citing that journal, with the sentence naming it in its text; `s194a_tds_covering_<tag>` cites it too, and `s194a_tds_coverage_<tag>` reads "not checked" where it read "none" (neither loan has interest, so there is no finding). The two LOAN-1 lines are gone. The book's comment says so.

## Declared behaviour difference: a TDS debit stays out of the TDS deducted (#1875 rule 4)

A voucher on the loan whose TDS lines net to a debit is no longer netted into `tds_on_loan_<tag>`, because a TDS debit can reverse an earlier deduction. A loan taken as Loan Cr 10,000 / Bank Dr 9,000 / TDS Payable Dr 1,000 used to make it -1,000. Each such voucher is named in that figure's text ("Left out: ..."), and it no longer appears among that figure's evidence. Its debits, summed, are a new figure, `tds_debited_on_loan_<tag>`, published only where there is one. LOAN-1 adds them back into its tie, because they moved the loan. A shape (a) voucher whose loans are credited takes its loans' shares here, so the two rules agree.

`tds_in_principal_<tag>` still holds a taken or repaid voucher's TDS of either sign. Where a debit is among it, its text is rewritten: the TDS counted on the loan on those vouchers, deductions positive and debits negative, its deductions inside the TDS deducted and its debits inside `tds_debited_on_loan_<tag>`. Elsewhere its text is the reference's. Two readings are left as they were. The date-aware `s194a_tds_covering_<tag>` still counts a debit as a reversal, as its text and the s.194A limit say. Its evidence and the TDS-seen finding's evidence still cite every voucher with TDS.

Rule 4 never makes a pass either. With debits out of the TDS deducted, a deduction beside a debit can look whole when the debit reversed it: a deduction and its reversal on one date, read deduction first, would read "covered" with nothing left deducted, and the same two read the other way would not. So where a loan has a TDS debit beside a deduction, the s.194A coverage reads "not checked", never "covered", "covered by amount, not by date" or "partly covered", whatever the amounts and read order. The coverage figure's text lists that reading. Where the interest is over the threshold, the s.194A finding lists the loan with the title above and the limit "Not checked: whether the TDS debit on <voucher> (tds_debited_on_loan_<tag>) reverses TDS deducted on this loan, and so whether what is left covers this interest.", and no TDS-seen finding fires. This holds for a small debit too (Round Loan below): the books do not say what any debit is. A TDS debit alone leaves nothing deducted and reads "none", as at the reference. Where the rules carry no s.194A rate, or the coverage is not computed, those readings stay.

The coverage is "not computed" (`coverage_open`) where a voucher listed as both crediting and debiting the loan carries its interest or TDS and any TDS is on the loan, a debit included, so a TDS debit alone opens it as at the reference. One case differs: a deduction and its reversal netting to nil on two other vouchers read "none" at the reference and now read "not computed", because that net is not "no TDS". The coverage figure's text is the reference's here. The not-computed finding's limit says a listed voucher's debit is in `tds_debited_on_loan_<tag>`, not in the TDS seen. The unit test `the_not_computed_finding_says_where_a_listed_vouchers_tds_debit_is` pins that limit against a control whose TDS on the listed voucher is a deduction.

A voucher whose TDS lines net to a debit is one debit by its net: a voucher with TDS Payable Cr 1,000 and TDS Payable Dr 200 on it is a deduction of 800, and one that nets to a debit is a debit of the net. A voucher on two loans on one side that is a debit is a debit on each loan, never a split deduction (`a_split_voucher_that_is_a_debit_is_not_a_split_deduction`: its coverage reads "none").

- Unit tests: `a_tds_debit_stays_out_of_the_tds_deducted_and_is_named` (the loan taken above, a TDS journal debiting TDS Payable, a deduction beside them, and a control with no debit; coverage "not checked"); `a_deduction_beside_a_tds_debit_is_never_read_as_covering_the_interest` (a deduction fully reversed on one date, in each read order, and two deductions with one reversed, the net short: each "not checked", listed, the debit named, no TDS-seen finding; a debit alone reads "none"); `any_tds_on_a_loan_with_a_listed_voucher_leaves_the_coverage_not_computed` (a deduction and its reversal, a debit alone, and the control with no TDS); `tds_debited_across_two_loans_on_one_side_is_each_loans_own_line` (rules 3 and 4 together).
- `edge-books/loans_interest_principal_tds_nets_nil.json`: the loan taken carrying a TDS debit of 100000 is left out. `tds_on_loan_<tag>` reads 100000 where it read 0, citing the repayment only, and `tds_debited_on_loan_<tag>` 100000 cites the loan taken. `s194a_tds_coverage_<tag>` reads "not checked" where it read "none" (no interest, so there is no finding). `tds_in_principal_<tag>` stays 0, with the debit wording above in its text, and LOAN-1 stays silent. The note `loans-tds-in-principal-and-nil-lines-1259.md` gives this book's reading at the reference and points here.
- `edge-books/loans_interest_phase_a_s194a.json`, Dated Loan: the reversal of the duplicate deduction is left out. `tds_on_loan_<tag>` reads 2000000 where it read 1000000, and `tds_debited_on_loan_<tag>` reads 1000000. Coverage reads "not checked" where it read "covered by amount, not by date", and the s.194A finding takes the not-checked title and limit, naming the reversal.
- `edge-books/loans_interest_tds_coverage.json`, Round Loan: the 50-paise reversal is left out. `tds_on_loan_<tag>` reads 100050 where it read 100000, and `tds_debited_on_loan_<tag>` reads 50. Coverage reads "not checked" where it read "covered". The TDS-seen finding is gone, the loan is listed in its place with the not-checked limit naming the reversal, and `s194a_tds_over_threshold_lender_count` reads 3 where it read 2.

## Goldens

Each moved golden is the crate's output for the parts named above, spliced into the reference's golden with the reference's key order (`kind`, `id`, `label` in each evidence object), each text's hash computed as `canonical::sha16` computes it. Nothing else in it changed. `edge.loans_interest_nil_line_interest_journal.loans_interest.json` no longer moves: it is the reference's golden byte for byte again. Their byte rows stay where they were, in `batch-d1.md` and `loans-tds-in-principal-and-nil-lines-1259.md`. Those notes' statements that the goldens regenerate byte-identical at the reference hold except for these parts.

## Not checked

- How often any of these shapes occurs on real books, or on a real Tally read.
- Whether a TDS debit on a real book is a reversal, a refund or something else. The figure names the voucher so the CA can tell.
- The reference engine on these books.
- Shape (a) with a TDS ledger that is also a loan's interest ledger or a shared one: such a ledger is not a TDS line in this test, so the voucher is not shape (a).
